title: Resume vs CV: what is the difference in the US?
desc: In the US, a resume and a CV are not the same thing. Learn when to use each one, how long they should be and what goes in them.
blocks: In most of the world, "CV" simply means the document you send with a job application. In the United States, the two words mean different things.
A resume is a short, focused summary of your experience, usually one page and two at most. It is what you send for almost every job in the private sector, and you tailor it to each role.

In the US, a CV is a long, complete record of an academic career: publications, research, teaching, grants, conferences. It is used for academic, research and some medical positions, and it can run many pages.
Applying to a company, a store, a hospital (non-research role), a startup: a resume.
Applying for a faculty, research or fellowship position: a CV.
Applying abroad: check the country's conventions. In the UK and Australia, a "CV" is close to a US resume.
